newsitem.title: UK: Report sees online shopping on rise in Europe.
newsitem.headline: Report sees online shopping on rise in Europe.

text.p: The amount consumers spend in online shopping in Europe is likely to grow to $3.23 billion in 2001 from current levels around $96 million, according to a report by research group Datamonitor published on Monday.
A statement on the report, "Consumer Online Shopping," said the "chief driver of growth will be the improved quantity and variety of shops available online, and the value that they offer."
It added that new measures to improve security of payments will also encourage shoppers to use the Internet online facilities.
Around 33 million European homes, seven percent of the total, will shop online by 2001, up from under one percent currently, Datamonitor added.
Germany currently dominates the online market, with $73 million of sales, likely to rise to $1.41 billion by 2001, Datamonitor said.
In Germany, mail order companies have a strong hold for clothes and household electronics sold online, Datamonitor said, but added that the market is likely to change.
"The Internet favours products which require information collection and comparison," the statement said.
Datamonitor suggested travel products such as flights, holidays and hotels, would account for 35 percent of consumer spending online by 2001.
Food and drink will become more popular online shopping areas as retailers solve problems over home delivery, Datamonitor said.
